Title: Family of 85-year-old Sydney man kidnapped by mistake say they are ‘living through a nightmare’
Date: 2026-02-17

Content: “Chris is a devoted father, brother, uncle, and grandfather. He is deeply loved, gentle, and the kindest person we know – someone who would never hurt a fly.” The family, in their statement released through NSW police, requested privacy as they waited “for some form of closure or resolution”. “This is an extraordinarily distressing time, and we need space to support one another and focus on navigating what comes next. Det Acting Supt Andrew Marks said on Monday that police believed Baghsarian was still alive. “This is not a typical crime,” he said at the time. “The offenders have got the wrong person. They were intending to take somebody but … they have kidnapped the wrong person.” Marks said Baghsarian’s family hadn’t received any ransom. “In a normal kidnapping case, we would be aware of a ransom.

chunk_b.text_snippet:
Title: Evidence linked to Sydney kidnap victim Chris Baghsarian, 85, discovered in burnt-out car as search continues
Date: 2026-02-23

Content: Police have said Baghsarian’s lack of personal links to any criminal or underworld activity was making the case difficult for investigators. No ransom had been demanded, leaving police to appeal directly to the kidnappers to return the grandfather to a safe location. Baghsarian’s family spoke publicly for the first time last week, describing the kidnapping as a surreal and harrowing ordeal. “Our family is living through a nightmare we never thought possible,” they said in a brief statement released via police.

initial_question.rag_input: How did the NSW police justify the status of the kidnapping investigation by February 23, 2026, after the family's February 17, 2026 appeal for privacy?
initial_question.question: How did the NSW police justify the status of the kidnapping investigation by February 23, 2026, after the family's February 17, 2026 appeal for privacy?
initial_question.answer: By February 23, 2026, police reported that the case remained difficult to solve because the victim had no criminal or underworld links, a status that persisted even after the family's February 17, 2026 statement where they requested privacy and confirmed the victim was a gentle man who would never hurt a fly, and police had already identified the kidnapping as a case of mistaken identity involving no ransom.
